name: 10 Days Tours From Marrakech Imperial Cities
seoTitle: Perfect 10 Days Tours From Marrakech to Imperial Cities
seoDescription: Atlas Private Tours offers you an unforgetable 10 Days Tour from Marrakech. Are you ready to take this journey with a local Moroccan travel Agency!
overview: Embark on an unforgettable 10-day journey through the heart of Morocco, starting and ending in the vibrant city of Marrakech. This immersive itinerary blends rich cultural heritage, imperial cities, desert adventures, and spectacular landscapes. From the bustling souks of Fes to the vast dunes of Merzouga, from Roman ruins to kasbahs, each day reveals a new facet of Morocco’s charm. Travel comfortably with an expert guide and driver, enjoy local cuisine, stay in authentic accommodations, and experience the warmth of Berber hospitality.
Whether you're strolling through the medinas, riding camels across golden dunes, or capturing sunset views from the Atlas Mountains, this tour promises an enriching and diverse Moroccan adventure.
highlights: Guided city tour of Marrakech , including Djemaa el-Fna, Bahia Palace, and Saadian Tombs
Day trip to the scenic Ourika Valley and visit to Berber villages
Visit to the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca
Exploration of Rabat , including the Mausoleum of Mohammed V and Kasbah des Oudaias
Guided tours of the imperial cities Meknes and Fes , with visits to historical mosques and medersas
Walk through the ancient Roman ruins of Volubilis
Drive through the Middle Atlas Mountains , cedar forests of Azrou, and stops in Ifrane and Midelt
Camel ride and overnight stay in a luxury desert camp in Merzouga , including campfire dinner and music
Scenic visit to Todra Gorge and overnight in the Dades Valley
Stops in Rose Valley and Skoura’s palm groves
Visit to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Ait Benhaddou
Crossing of the High Atlas Mountains via Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2260m)
Comfortable accommodations and professional driver/guide throughout the journey

itinerary.title: Arrival to Marrakech
itinerary.text: The first day in Morocco starts with our guide and the driver. We transfer the toy from the Hotel to the stunning Ourika Valley to see traditional Berber villages, we’ll have lunch and free time to walk around Marrakech, where we will spend our night.

itinerary.title: Marrakech tourism
itinerary.text: Today we make a tour in the city with a local guide, visit the tomb, the Palace, and the medina, and the famous Djemaa el-Fna in Marrakech, and after taking some photos for these incredible places, as night falls we’ll have dinner and spend the night in Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Casablanca – Rabat
itinerary.text: We start the day in Casablanca where we have a guided tour around the impressive  Hassan II Mosque, then we stop in order to have some delicious Moroccan lunch, after having lunch we head to Rabat, where we will visit the mausoleum of Mohammed V and Kasbah des Oudaias and we spend the night in this beautiful place.

itinerary.title: Rabat, Meknes, Volubilis – Fes
itinerary.text: This day starts at Volubilis , Morocco’s largest and best preserved Roman ruins, then visit the third Imperial city “Meknes”, and enjoy the amazing landscapes and views, after a short time in travel we reach to Fez, the oldest of the imperial cities and we spend the night here.

itinerary.title: Fes Tourism
itinerary.text: Today is a full day tour with a local guide in Fes, we visit the MedersaBou Inania, the Mausoleum of Moulay Idriss and the Andalusian and the  Quaraoiyin mosques and take some photos in these beautiful landscapes, then we visit the Nejjarine Museum Square with its fountain of the 18th century, Fes medina is a maze of more than 9000 small narrow cobbled streets, finally we spend our night in this amazing madina.

itinerary.title: Ifrane – Midelt -Erfoud – Rissani – Merzouga desert
itinerary.text: We start this day at Ifrane “the Lion City” in the southeast direction, we prefer to rest for lunch before we continue to the Middle Atlas mountains, then we drive by the cedar forest of Azrou, we are still in the deep south in  Errachidia in order to take photos and enjoy interesting views of the gorges and Oasis zigzag path , then relax on the edge of the sand dunes . It’ll be an incredible experience swimming in the pool house guests, while in the vastness of the desert that extends in front of us, after lunch we have free time to explore the dunes or take a tour in the desert in camel, In the evening we have dinner around a campfire, and sleep in tents.

itinerary.title: Merzouga –  Gorges Todra – Dades valley and ravine
itinerary.text: Today we go back to meet our driver, then travel through the vast rural areas, seeing the impressive landscape changed again. Local conditions permitting, we visit the impressive Todra Gorge before continuing to Dades Gorge, finally we spend the night and have the dinner in Dades Gorges.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge – Rose Valley – Skoura – AitBenhaddou  – Atlas mountains – Marrakech
itinerary.text: We start the day with the breakfast then enjoy the green landscapes course to Ouarzazate, the gateway to the  Sahara, and now famous in Hollywood in the desert, due to the number of famous movies that have been made. We drives along the river Ounila which is known for its Kasbahs, we visit then fortified city of AitBenhaddou, declared a World Heritage Site by  UNESCO since 1987 , along the ancient caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech in the current Morocco, we are jumping over the 2260m Tizi n’Tichka and then down to the plains, in the afternoon we arrive to Marrakech in order to spend the last night in the Hotel together.

The tour ends after breakfast since it is the last day, so we transfer to the airport.
For those arriving by plane at the end of the day, you’ll have the chance to take an  optional excursion to the Ourika Valley, or for those who adhere to the Atlas Trek (subject to flight schedules ), the journey starts after breakfast and ends in the afternoon, around 5  pm.

name: 4 Days Atlas Tour from Fes to Marrakech via Merzouga Desert
seoTitle: Top 4 Days Atlas Private Tour from Fes to Marrakech via Merzouga
seoDescription: Your best way to explore the Morocca Sahara in short time is through this 4 Days Atlas Private Tour from Fes to Marrakech via Merzouga. 2026
overview: Experience the beauty and diversity of Morocco on this 4-Day Fez to Marrakech Desert Tour . From the lush Middle Atlas Mountains to the golden Sahara dunes, this journey combines breathtaking landscapes, rich culture, and authentic Berber experiences.

Your adventure begins in Fez, traveling through the charming town of Ifrane, often called the “Switzerland of Morocco”, and the cedar forests of Azrou, where wild monkeys roam freely. Traverse the Middle Atlas Mountains and the scenic Ziz Valley, passing traditional Berber villages before arriving at the edge of the majestic Erg Chebbi dunes in Merzouga.

Spend the evening under a nomadic Bedouin tent, enjoying camel treks, desert music, and the star-filled Sahara sky. The tour continues through Rissani, Todra Gorges, Dades Valley, and the Valley of Roses before reaching Ouarzazate and the iconic Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , a UNESCO World Heritage site and filming location for blockbuster movies. The journey concludes as you return to Marrakech via the High Atlas Mountains, witnessing picturesque villages, terraced farms, and spectacular mountain vistas.
This tour is ideal for travelers seeking adventure, culture, and the magic of Morocco’s most famous landscapes.
highlights: Explore the Middle Atlas Mountains and cedar forests of Azrou, home to wild monkeys.
Cross the scenic Ziz Valley with its dramatic gorges and palm oases.
Discover Erfoud , the capital of fossils, with its fascinating fossil shops.
Experience the Sahara Desert at Erg Chebbi , including camel rides and overnight in a traditional nomadic tent.
Visit Khamlia village , home of the Gnawa music and dancing traditions.
Witness a magical sunrise over the Sahara dunes and climb the dunes for stunning panoramic views.
Explore the largest traditional souk in southern Morocco at Rissani.
Drive through Todra Gorges and Dades Valley , known for dramatic rock formations and the Valley of Roses.
Stay in Ouarzazate , Morocco’s “Hollywood of Africa,” and visit its film studios.
Walk through the historic Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , featured in Gladiator , Sahara , and The Kingdom of Heaven .
Return to Marrakech via the High Atlas Mountains , enjoying breathtaking views and Berber villages along the way.

itinerary.title: Merzouga grand Tour – Erg Chebbi

At the end of the day we’ll arrive to Ouarzazate and spend the night in the Hotel.

We’ll continue driving to Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka, where we see Berber villages and farms on the side of the mountains. name: 9 Days Tour from Casablanca Rabat Fes and Marrakech
seoTitle: Perfect 9 Days Tour from Casablanca Rabat Fes and Marrakech
seoDescription: Discover Morocco with Atlas Private Tours on a 9 Days Tour from Casablanca Rabat Fes and Marrakech. A perfect blend of culture, history, and ...
highlights: Casablanca:  Visit the iconic Hassan II Mosque on the Atlantic Ocean.
Rabat:  Explore the Royal Palace, Hassan Tower, Mohamed V Mausoleum & the Kasbah of Oudayas.
Meknes:  Discover Bab El Mansour, Moulay Ismail Mausoleum, and the grand Medina.
Volubilis:  Wander through the impressive Roman ruins and mosaics.
Fes:  Lose yourself in the medieval Medina, with visits to the Bou Inania Madrasa, Karaouine Mosque, Nejjarine Fountain, tanneries, and bustling souks.
Ifrane & Azrou:  Enjoy the charm of “Morocco’s Switzerland” and the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas.
Ouzoud Waterfalls:  Witness one of Morocco’s most beautiful cascades before heading to Marrakech.
Marrakech:  Visit Koutoubia Mosque, Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, Majorelle Garden, and experience the energy of Jemaa el-Fna Square.
Essaouira:  Relax in this seaside town, famous for its medina, port, seafood, and argan oil cooperatives.

itinerary.title: Casablanca
itinerary.text: At your arrival to Casablanca Airport. You’ll meet our guide/driver ,then we will go to the Hotel.

itinerary.title: Casablanca  Rabat
itinerary.text: This day starts with breakfast at the Hotel, then we will have a short tour in the city of Casablanca, it is the largest city in Morocco; it is the heart of commerce and industry , surely we will visit Hassan II mosque, that is-two thirds of it, built on water alongside the Atlantic Ocean, then we stop to have lunch in Rabat, then continue the tour with a visit to the the Royal Palace, The Mausoleum of Mohamed V and the Hassan Tower, the incomplete minaret mosque initiated by The Almohad ruler, Yaacoub al-Mansour, and The Kasbah of Oudaias, there are white houses with blue painted parapets located near to the Atlantic coast, this exciting day ends up in the Hotel.

itinerary.title: Rabat  Meknes  Fes
itinerary.text: Today we will travel to Meknes then to the nearby city Fes, after we’ll have our breakfast at the Hotel. Meknes is the third Imperial city of Morocco with its famous doors, it is known as “The Versailles of Morocco. Followed by a visit to the Bab El Mansour, one of the most beautiful gateways. Then continue the tour by visiting the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail. After that a visit to the Old and new Medina , after eating a delicious lunch. Later on you will visit the village of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun which is a place of pilgrimage for Moroccans. And we will discover the ancient Roman ruins of Volubulis. Finally we will go to Fes. And have a very nice and delicious traditional Moroccan dinner before leaving the Riad or Hotel.

itinerary.title: Fes
itinerary.text: This day will be the a historyl day, because we have a tour in the Royal city of Fès, after having breakfast we will go to the medieval Medina (old city) with its ramparts and narrow streets that were declared as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1981, with its fabulous 16th Century Merinid Tombs Ruins, then we visit the Bouanania and the Attarine Medersas constructed in the early 14th century by the Merinides, the Karaouine Mosque (The ancient educational center of Islamic learning), and the Nejjarine Marble Fountain, this will be end up by having lunch at a typical Moroccan restaurant, and after taking some rest we will continue to visit the decorated gate of Bab Boujeloud, the medieval tanneries, the Royal Palace .Then visit of the Souks (local markets) where merchants and craftsmen sell their hand-made jewelry, leather goods, copperware and pottery, and finally we arrive the Hotel for dinner and to have a goof night after a full busy day.

itinerary.title: Fes  Ifran  Azrou  Beni Mellal  Ouzoud Waterfalls  Marrakech
itinerary.text: The tour today is towards to Marrakech (the pearl of the south) through the Middle Atlas via Ifran“known as The Moroccan Switzerland”, we see a stone lion before we continue on Azrou “a Berber town known for its green tiled roofs” and have our lunch in Beni Mellal, then we may visit the impressive Ouzoud Waterfalls then the final station is Marrakech where we really enjoy our evening meal and spend the night in a Riad or hotel.

itinerary.title: Marrakech
itinerary.text: This day is devoted to the southern fabulous city of Marrakech, starting with a short visit to the Koutoubia Mosque and admire its tower, the Majorelle Garden; a botanical garden with its varied plants, the 16th century Saadian Tombs; all decorated in colorful mosaic tiles, the 19th century Bahia Palace with its beautiful eastern Architecture, we take photos in these attractive places, then we’ll eat lunch. The afternoon is nearby so it is the suitable time for visiting the fascinating Souks and the narrow alleys around the Djemâa El-Fna Square, and buy some of traditional objects, evening will last longer within the lights of cafes, snake charmers, singers, acrobats, dancers, narrators and story-tellers – moving from one group to another, we can now have dinner and go to sleep after this fabulous busy day.

itinerary.title: Marrakech  Essaouira
itinerary.text: We eat our breakfast as usual, then we will leave this fantastic southern red city of Marrakech towards Essaouira, in order to visit an Argan factory run by women and get to know about the process of making Argan oil, you must have heard of the Moroccan Argan and the wide uses of this fully needed product, after that we go to see the port of the Coastal tourist town of Essaouira , and have a seafood meal in the medina, we get to explore the city and the places alone, swim and relax on the beach, this relaxing will make you surrender to sleep in a Riad or hotel

itinerary.title: Essaouira  Safi  Oualidia  El Jadida  Casablanca

highlights: Discover the majestic Hassan II Mosque, Casablanca's most iconic landmark
Explore the historic treasures of Rabat, Morocco’s elegant capital
Wander through the UNESCO-listed Roman ruins of Volubilis and admire Meknes’ imperial beauty
Dive into the heart of Fes, Morocco’s cultural and spiritual epicenter
Journey through the scenic Atlas Mountains, filled with panoramic vistas

itinerary.title: Casablanca – Rabat – Chefchaouen
itinerary.text:
Begin your Moroccan adventure with a visit to one of the largest mosques in the world, perched beside the Atlantic Ocean. Its grandeur and design offer a powerful introduction to Moroccan craftsmanship. Then head north to Rabat, the capital city, where you’ll explore significant monuments such as a majestic royal gate, a royal mausoleum, and a centuries-old kasbah that overlooks the ocean.
Following lunch, your journey continues through picturesque landscapes until you reach Chefchaouen, nestled in the Rif Mountains. Known for its tranquil blue-washed medina, this town is a haven for photographers and explorers. Spend the evening enjoying the peaceful atmosphere and discovering its charming streets.

itinerary.title: Chefchaouen – Volubilis – Fes
itinerary.text:
Enjoy a relaxed morning in Chefchaouen, strolling through its winding alleys and traditional artisan shops. The town offers a blend of local craftsmanship, mountain scenery, and spiritual calm. Afterward, travel south toward Volubilis , one of Morocco’s most impressive archaeological sites.
Wander among ancient Roman ruins, where beautifully preserved mosaics, arches, and columns hint at the city’s past glory. Later, head toward Fes, one of Morocco’s oldest and most spiritually significant cities, where you'll settle in for the evening.

itinerary.title: Fes – Full Day Guided Exploration
itinerary.text:
Dedicate your day to immersing yourself in the rich heritage of Fes. Begin with a look at the grand gates of the Royal Palace, then step into the labyrinthine old medina, a UNESCO World Heritage Site , through its iconic Blue Gate.
Wander through a maze of souks and historical landmarks, including a splendid Islamic school, an intricately decorated fountain, and the colorful tanneries. Visit the world’s oldest university still in operation and experience the spiritual ambiance that permeates the city. Later, explore the Jewish quarter and enjoy panoramic views from one of the city’s ancient fortresses.

itinerary.title: Fes – Ifrane – Cedar Forest – Midelt – Ziz Valley – Merzouga
itinerary.text:
Start your journey toward the desert by crossing through Morocco’s mountainous heartland. Visit Ifrane, a clean and peaceful town often compared to alpine resorts due to its European-style architecture and snowy winters.
Continue to a nearby cedar forest, where native monkeys roam freely, before stopping in a mountain town for lunch. As you descend into the south, marvel at the dramatic scenery of the Ziz Valley, filled with palm groves and ochre cliffs. By late afternoon, reach the edge of the Sahara in Merzouga.
Here, mount a camel and ride into the dunes to catch a glorious desert sunset. Your evening is spent at a desert camp under a canopy of stars, with traditional music around the fire and a taste of Berber hospitality.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Rissani – Erfoud – Todra Gorges – Dades Valley
itinerary.text:
Begin with a magical sunrise over the dunes, followed by breakfast. Depart the desert and visit a bustling desert town known for its traditional market and ancient roots. Continue to Erfoud, where local artisans transform fossils into beautiful decor pieces.
Journey through palm-lined villages toward the dramatic Todra Gorges, a deep canyon carved by natural forces and beloved by climbers. Take time to walk through its towering cliffs, then head to the Dades Valley. Here, you’ll explore fascinating rock formations and enjoy sweeping views before settling in for the night.

itinerary.title: Dades – Rose Valley – Skoura – Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Haddou – Marrakech
itinerary.text:
Travel through a region famous for rose cultivation, especially vibrant in the spring months. Stop in the oasis of Skoura, known for its palm groves and kasbahs. Arrive in Ouarzazate, often called the “Hollywood of Africa” due to its film studios and cinematic history.
Your next stop is the legendary fortified village of Ait Ben Haddou, a UNESCO-listed site with earthen clay architecture and a storybook charm. It has been featured in many global films and series. Cross the majestic High Atlas Mountains via a scenic mountain pass, winding through Berber villages and rugged terrain. Arrive in Marrakech by evening.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Casablanca
itinerary.text:
Depending on your departure time, spend the morning exploring the must-see sights of Marrakech. Visit its enchanting gardens, historic mosques, elegant palaces, and bustling medina streets filled with artisans and storytellers.
If time allows, enjoy more of the city’s ambiance before heading back to Casablanca via the highway, concluding your 7-day Moroccan journey with unforgettable memories.

faqs.q: How long is the camel ride in Merzouga?
faqs.a: Usually between 1 to 1.5 hours each way, depending on your camp’s location in the dunes. Travelers who prefer not to ride camels can request a 44 transfer to the camp.

faqs.q: What type of accommodations are included?
faqs.a: You’ll stay in a mix of traditional riads, kasbah-style hotels, and one night in a desert camp (standard or luxury, depending on your choice).

faqs.q: Is the tour suitable for families or older travelers?
faqs.a: Yes. The private nature of the tour makes it flexible. The pace can be adjusted, and camel rides or long walks can be replaced with 44 transport if needed.
Not fully. Cities and some flat areas can handle strollers, but medinas, kasbahs, and especially the desert dunes are not stroller-friendly. A baby carrier is recommended for rougher terrain.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to do this trip?
faqs.a: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer the most pleasant weather. Summer can be very hot in the desert, while winter nights can be cold.

faqs.q: How much driving is involved each day?
faqs.a: On average, you’ll spend 4–6 hours on the road daily, with plenty of scenic and cultural stops along the way to break up the journey.

faqs.q: What should I pack for the desert overnight stay?
faqs.a: Comfortable clothing, a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, and a warm layer for the evening. Most camps provide blankets, but it’s good to have a jacket in colder months.

itinerary.title: From Marrakech to Dades Valley via High Atlas Mountains & Ait Benhaddou ( Driving Time: 6.5 hours)
itinerary.text:
Your journey begins at 8:00 AM with a private driver/guide picking you up from your accommodation in Marrakech. Departing the bustling city, you’ll traverse the majestic High Atlas Mountains, home to picturesque snow-covered peaks for most of the year. As you ascend the famous Tizi n’Tichka Pass at 2,260 meters, you'll be treated to sweeping views of traditional Amazigh (Berber) villages perched along the mountain slopes, many of them built from adobe and stone along narrow riverbeds.
A guided tour awaits at the historic village of Ait Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site . From here, continue to the cinematic town of Ouarzazate, dubbed “The Hollywood of Africa,” where you can optionally visit the Atlas Film Studios. Pass through the scenic palm groves of Skoura and the Valley of Roses before arriving in Boumalne Dades. Here, you'll settle in for the evening.

You’ll then pass through Merzouga village en route to Khamlia, a small village known for its Gnawa heritage. The locals, descendants of sub-Saharan African slaves, will welcome you with a performance of their traditional spiritual music, deeply rooted in rhythm and healing.
Next, take a scenic drive around the perimeter of the Erg Chebbi dunes with several stops for photos. One of the highlights will be visiting a nomadic family living in tents, an authentic chance to learn about their daily life while sharing tea with them. After a local lunch, return to your desert Riad or Kasbah for the evening to relax and recharge.
Overnight at a Riad

Your journey then flows through the dramatic Dades Valley and cinematic landscapes of Ouarzazate, before reaching the colorful streets of Marrakech. After diving into the city’s rich culture and vibrant souks, you’ll unwind in the charming coastal town of Essaouira, known for its blend of Portuguese architecture, art, and ocean breeze. The adventure concludes back in Casablanca with warm memories of Morocco's diversity and soul.

itinerary.title: Casablanca – Rabat – Chefchaouen
itinerary.text:
Your morning begins with a visit to the iconic seaside mosque, a symbol of modern Moroccan craftsmanship. From there, you’ll journey to the political capital, Rabat, to admire its grand mausoleum, royal gates, and fortified kasbah with ocean views.
After lunch, you’ll drive north through rolling hills and quaint villages until you reach the picturesque town of Chefchaouen . Known for its serene blue alleyways, this mountain gem is perfect for evening strolls and cultural immersion.

itinerary.title: Chefchaouen – Roman Ruins of Volubilis – Fes
itinerary.text:
Spend the morning discovering Chefchaouen at your leisure. With its calming blue walls, artisan shops, and peaceful plazas, the town invites you to slow down and enjoy the details. You can explore small museums, historic kasbahs, and panoramic viewpoints.
Later, you'll travel to the Roman ruins of Volubilis, a remarkably preserved ancient city with mosaics and arches that offer a window into Morocco’s deep past. After exploring the site, the day ends in Fes, where your next cultural chapter begins.

itinerary.title: Guided Exploration of Fes
itinerary.text:
Today is fully dedicated to the cultural treasures of Fes. Begin with a visit to the monumental gate of the Royal Palace before stepping into the UNESCO-listed old city. Navigating the medieval medina, you'll explore sacred sites, bustling souks, and traditional workshops.
Key stops include historic theological schools, ancient fountains, leather tanneries, and the oldest functioning university in the world. Beyond the walls of the medina, a visit to the Jewish quarter and a panoramic viewpoint offers broader insight into Fes' layered identity.

itinerary.title: Fes – Middle Atlas – Merzouga (Sahara)
itinerary.text:
After breakfast, the route takes you through the Middle Atlas Mountains. First stop: a charming mountain town often dubbed the “Switzerland of Morocco” for its alpine-style architecture and lush surroundings. You’ll continue to a nearby cedar forest to meet the wild Barbary monkeys.
Enjoy a midday break in a small town known for its quiet charm before venturing deeper into Morocco’s south. As the scenery changes to desert plateaus, you’ll arrive at the gateway to the Sahara by late afternoon. Here, your camel caravan awaits to carry you across the dunes at sunset.
The evening is spent in a desert camp, where traditional rhythms and a starlit sky make for a magical night.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Todra Gorges – Dades Valley
itinerary.text:
Begin your day with a peaceful sunrise over the dunes before heading to a traditional town known for its historic trade market. Later, you’ll pass through areas famed for fossils and artisan workshops, offering insight into Morocco’s prehistoric heritage.
The journey then leads to the towering cliffs of Todra Gorges, where you can walk between steep canyon walls and enjoy lunch surrounded by natural beauty. The day ends in the Dades Valley, where rock formations and scenic viewpoints create a breathtaking finale.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley – Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Haddou – Marrakech
itinerary.text:
Following breakfast, you’ll continue through fragrant valleys known for their rose products and lively springtime festivals. Then, pass through palm-dotted landscapes toward the cinematic town of Ouarzazate, often referred to as the “Hollywood of Morocco.”
Next comes a highlight of the trip: the fortified village of Ait Ben Haddou . Its earthen clay architecture and ancient alleyways transport you back in time. After exploring the kasbah, you’ll drive through the spectacular mountain pass of Tizi-N-Tichka before arriving in the bustling city of Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Guided Tour of Marrakech
itinerary.text:
Today you’ll explore the legendary Red City with a knowledgeable guide. Visit peaceful gardens, majestic mosques, and palaces that echo with centuries of history. Marvel at the intricate artistry of tombs and courtyards that reflect Morocco’s rich design heritage.
In the afternoon, get lost in the vibrant souks, where every turn brings spices, textiles, and hand-crafted treasures. After lunch near the main square, enjoy some free time to continue exploring on your own or simply relax in a local café.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Essaouira
itinerary.text:
Leave the lively streets of Marrakech behind and head west toward the Atlantic coast. Arriving in Essaouira, you'll be greeted by cool ocean breezes and the charm of a fortified coastal medina. Known for its laid-back energy and artsy vibe, the town invites you to explore its port, watch local artisans at work, or simply unwind along the sea wall.
Essaouira’s architecture, seafood, and historic ambiance make it a perfect destination to wind down your journey.

itinerary.title: Essaouira – Return to Casablanca
itinerary.text:
On your final day of this mesmerizing 10-day Morocco Tour Itinerary from Casablanca, enjoy a relaxing breakfast before your transfer back to Casablanca. Depending on your flight time or travel plans, we’ll ensure a smooth and timely arrival at either the airport or your accommodation.
Note: If your departure is from Marrakech instead, transportation will be arranged accordingly to meet your schedule comfortably.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Ait Ben Haddou – Ouarzazate
itinerary.text: In the first day we departs from Marrakech at 8am and travel over the stunning High Atlas Mountains through Tizi n’Tichka (alt 2260 m). Then we visit the Argon oil cooperative and stop there to take photos and enjoy the landscape. We’ll have lunch in a local restaurant, in the afternoon we visit the UNESCO World Heritage site Ait Ben Haddou. Then go to Ouarzazate for dinner and spend our night in a traditional Hotel.

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate – Draa Valley – Merzouga
itinerary.text: In the early morning and after having breakfast we visit the Taourirt Kasbah, then travel through the scenic road along the the Djebel Sarhro mountain range, down to the oasis and kasbahs of the Draa valley and along the Draa, Morocco’s largest river on our way to the desert, before we passe through many Berber villages including Agdz and N’kob where we search at a local restaurant in order to have a lunch , after this long morning, arrival is at Merzouga, at night we will go to the Hotel to have the dinner and rest.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Khamlia – Rissani – Erg Chebbi (Night In Nomadic Tent)
itinerary.text: We will devote this day for the desert region, we’ll get to know nomad’s way of life and the amazing changing contrasts of the desert, we then visit the ‘black village’ of Khamlia to see the Gnawa musicians, for lunch we have a traditional Berber pizza in the ancient capital of Rissani, between lunch and the afternoon we visit traditional markets, later on, we go back to the hotel to be prepared for camel riding for almost 90 minutes over the Erg Chebbi desert dunes to the desert camp, then we have a traditional Tagine dinner and delicious mint tea while watching the stars and the rising moon in the amazing desert, finally we spend the night in a traditional nomad tent.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Todra Gorge – Dades Gorge
itinerary.text: Today we shall wake up early in order to see the spectacular sunrise over the dunes of the Sahara then we go back to the Hotel for breakfast and a shower. After breakfast, we travel via Erfoud, behind the High Atlas Mountains on route to the Todra Gorges. And we take a short walks up in the towering Todra Gorges before continuing along the picturesque river valleys towards Dades Gorge. In the afternoon, after lunch we walk in the Dades Gorge. And at night we go back to Hotel and have a dinner before going to sleep there.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge – Telouet – Marrakech
itinerary.text: The last day will start with a walk in the gorge where we gaze at the Dades Valley through El Kelaa Magona and oasis of Skoura then have lunch. After lunch in Ouarzazate we descend the High Atlas Mountains to visit Telouet and the Kasbah el Glaoui. And finally we arrive to Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Fes

itinerary.title: Fes
itinerary.text: This day starts with a visit to the spiritual capital of Morocco at around 8:00, the old medina , the Royal Palace , the Mellah (Jewish quarter), Bab Boujloud entrance, then we explore the greater medina from all over Morocco “el-Bali”, and madrasa (Koranic school) of the 17th century, etc, after that we’ll have lunch and then continue visiting Fes.

itinerary.title: Fes – Volubilis – Meknes-Fes
itinerary.text: In this morning we visit he mausoleum of Moulay Idris, the founder of Fes in the sixth century, after having breakfast, on our way we visit the magnificent roman ruins of Volubilis. Then continue our journey to Meknes in order to visit the mausoleum of Moulay Ismail (ancestor of the current King Mohammed VI of Morocco) and the royal palace, and the enormous Elhdim up to the gates of the city, Bab Mansour, finally we go back to the Hotel in order to spend the night after a tiring day.

itinerary.title: Fes- Sahara Desert
itinerary.text: Today we will go to the Sahara desert, but first of all we shall have our breakfast then pass over the Middle Atlas and stop in a Berber village, its people are well known for their hospitality, we can take some photos there, it is an ancient fabulous place, before continuing the journey in the Ziz valley and reach the dunes of Erg Chebbi we will have lunch, there we can go with camels to the desert until the camp located in the heart of the dunes, when we climb the dunes we see an incredible landscape of sunset and enjoy drinking tea, finally we spend the night in the berber tent with traditional music around campfire.

itinerary.title: Sahara – Erfoud – Ouarzazate
itinerary.text: Wake up early in order to climb the dunes and admire the majestic sunrise over them, we can also take the camel back to the Hotel and have our breakfast there, then we go to Erfoud towards the west and the Todra Gorges, then continue to Dades Valley after having our lunch, followed by a visit to the City of Roses, at the end of the day we arrive to Ouarzazate where we spend night in a Riad or Hotel.

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate – Marrakech
itinerary.text: Today we will visit the Atlas Studios, known worldwide as the kasbah Taourirt which was the residence of the Glaoui family, after breakfast we go to visit the Kasbah of Ait Ben Hadou and Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains, we stop and take photos in every place we visit, there is beauty , finally we arrive to Riad or Hotel in Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Marrakech

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Dades gorges

Continue via Ouarzazate crossing the Valley of Roses, to get into the Dades Gorges, where the “route of the thousand kasbahs” begins, we can take a lot of photos there and enjoy breathtaking views, the places are really incredible, finishing at the Hotel in the Dades Valley to spend the night and have dinner.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorges – Todra Gorges – Merzouga
itinerary.text: Today starts with a Moroccan breakfast, after that we set off to the Todra Gorge, in order to take a pleasant walk through the impressive canyon walls higher than 200 meters, in the road towards the desert we passe through the palm grove of Tafilalet, upon arrival we ride camels to go on an hour and a half route, trekking through the sand dunes to the heart of the desert to watch the beautiful sunset , enjoy the music of drums and the magical views, finally have dinner and Moroccan tea, while looking at the immense starry sky then spend the night at the Berber tents.
